{{2021–22 Southeastern Conference men's basketball standings}}

The '''2021–22 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team''' represented [[Auburn University]] during the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]] as a member of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. The team's head coach was [[Bruce Pearl]] in his eighth season at Auburn.  The team played their home games at [[Neville Arena]]{{efn|name=arena}} in [[Auburn, Alabama]]. They finished the season 28–6, 15–3 in SEC play to finish as regular season champions. As the No. 1 seed, they were defeated by No. 8 seed [[2021–22 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] in the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 2 seed in the Midwest Region, where they defeated [[2021–22 Jacksonville State Gamecocks men's basketball team|Jacksonville State]] in the First Round before being upset by [[2021–22 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]] in the Second Round.

On January 24, 2022, the team was voted first in the [[AP Poll#Men's basketball|AP poll]] for the first time in program history, in the midst of a nineteen-game winning streak.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-24|title=Auburn No. 1 for first time in history of AP poll|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33139003/auburn-tigers-no-1-first-history-ap-top-25-men-basketball-poll|access-date=2022-02-08|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2020–21 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team]] finished the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]] 13–14, 7–11 in SEC play. Due to a self-imposed postseason ban following former assistant coach [[Chuck Person]]'s involvement in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]], the Tigers were ineligible to compete in the [[2021 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] and the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].

==Offseason==

===Departures===
Auburn lost five players from the [[2020–21 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|2020–21 team]]. Freshmen [[Sharife Cooper]] and [[JT Thor]] were selected in the [[2021 NBA Draft|NBA draft]], and Javon Franklin, Jamal Johnson, and [[Justin Powell]] transferred.
